Subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions + pricing (hit rates and effective $/1M)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jordan — good conversation and helpful context on Acme's expected chat usage. Per our ask, here's a short write-up of the caching assumptions we discussed and how those move the effective $/1M tokens in our pricing model. I copied Marcus and Aditya for any technical/contract clarifications.

Quick recap of Acme's usage notes from the call:
- Primary use: customer support assistant + guided product walkthroughs.
- Expected monthly input/output (tokens): ~250M tokens/month initially; target growth to ~1B tokens over 12 months.
- Typical session length: 150-600 tokens; many repeated prefixes (product prompts + user context) across sessions.
- SLA: 99.9% availability; budget-minded — targeting a combined infra + inference unit economics close to $X/1M tokens (open to guidance).

Caching assumptions we discussed:
- Prefix / static prompt caching: we expect a high reuse of the same prompt templates (product prompt + system instructions). Those are good candidates for prefix caching (server-side KV cache).
- Session KV caching: recent conversation tokens can be cached between requests for the same session id to avoid re-decoding the prefix repeatedly.
- TTL: for the pricing exercise we used a conservative TTL of 30 minutes for session cache and 24 hours for prefix cache.
- Hit rate guidance: we sketched a conservative baseline hit rate of 20% and an optimistic scenario of 50%+ for product teams with a lot of repeated prompts.

How we applied this to pricing (high level):
- Base list unit: $1,200 per 1M input+output tokens for the chosen model variant (this is the starting point for Dedicated pricing; we can create committed tiers).
- Effective cost = base_unit_price * (1 - cache_hit_rate). This assumes hits bypass expensive model execution; misses are billed at full unit rate. (We also model small overhead for cache management, included in the base price.)

Requested from you to move forward:
1) Can you confirm monthly token estimate (250M -> 1B) and any seasonality/peaks? The pricing workbook I attached has rows for low/expected/high.
2) Do you have a target effective $/1M tokens target or budget range we should aim for? (e.g., <$1,000/1M, $1,000-3,000/1M, etc.)
3) If we can schedule a short follow-up (30 min) with your infra lead next week, Marcus can walk through the prefix/session caching approach and confirm integration details.

Next steps from our side:
- I attached a pricing worksheet with scenarios (base price, hit rate, effective price). Marcus will prepare a short technical note on how prefix cache would be integrated with your session IDs.

Thanks — talk soon.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions + pricing (hit rates and effective $/1M)

Thanks — great questions. Quick answers and a few concrete scenarios so you can see the math. Marcus/Aditya feel free to chime in if I miss any nuance.

Answers to Jordan's technical Qs:
- Prompt ID: we prefer the customer provide a canonical prompt id where possible (reduces hash collision risk and makes cache control explicit). We can also compute hashes on our side if you can't emit ids, but that adds ~10-20ms and slightly reduces hit rate due to differences in normalization.
- Billing on cache hits: cached tokens are not re-processed by the model. We bill only for model-executed tokens. For retrieval-only hits (prefix fully satisfied from cache) effective model tokens = 0 for that request. For partial hits (e.g., cached prefix + new user tokens) we bill for the non-cached tokens. There is a small per-request retrieval overhead baked into the base price (no separate line-item).

Example unit economics (using the base price we discussed):
- Base model price (list): $1,200 per 1M tokens (input+output).
Scenarios (effective price per 1M tokens = base * (1 - hit_rate)):
- 0% hit (no caching): $1,200 / 1M tokens
- 20% hit: $960 / 1M tokens
- 40% hit: $720 / 1M tokens
- 60% hit: $480 / 1M tokens

Notes on assumptions used for these scenarios:
- Hit rate definition: fraction of model-executed tokens avoided because the content was served from cache. This includes prefix reuse and session KV hits under the TTLs noted earlier.
- Prefix cache effectiveness depends heavily on how many template prompts and system messages are identical across sessions. Teams with highly templated prompts typically see 30-60% prefix hit in practice.
- Session KV caching helps when users have repeated back-and-forth in short windows; it's more valuable for longer sessions.
- For blended deployments (mix of cached hits and misses at different times), we can model monthly effective price by weighting the scenarios by traffic percentage.

Worked example for Acme conservative month (250M tokens) at 20% hit:
- Gross model tokens billed = 250M * (1 - 0.20) = 200M billed tokens
- Cost = 200 * $1,200 / 1M = $240,000 for the month (model costs).

I attached the pricing worksheet with a low/expected/high tab — fill in your monthly token columns and the sheet will compute effective costs across hit-rate scenarios.

Next steps / proposal:
1) Please confirm the monthly token rows in the sheet (I circled the 250M conservative number).
2) If <$1,200/1M is the target, we should prioritize getting prefix IDs and focus on prompt normalization to move toward 40%+ hits; that should get you under $720/1M.
